title: 16_anchor (Trinity Anchor)
description: Trinity Anchor artifact for Step 16. Declares the full scope of a multi-milestone implementation, tracks which milestones own which FRs, and is the cross-milestone drift-detection surface. Does NOT carry a per-FR checklist — that detail lives in each 16a milestone plan. Does NOT carry execution or review sections — those are milestone-plan concerns.

allOf.description: Inherits shared step-base properties ($schema, id, owner, created_at, canonical_refs_used).

artifact_role.description: Identifies this artifact as the Trinity Anchor. Required. Enables validators to distinguish the anchor from 16a/16b/16c milestone plans without relying on file path heuristics. Must always be the string 'anchor' — any other value fails schema validation.

plan.description: Anchor-level plan: scope declaration, accumulated ambiguities, drift monitoring schedule, and milestone ownership registry.

summary.description: High-level scope summary for the full multi-milestone implementation.

functional_summary.description: 1–3 sentences describing the full implementation scope: the capability delivered, primary actors, and key constraints across all milestones. Example: 'Implements JWT authentication and session management for the mobile API across two milestones. Covers token issuance, validation, and revocation. Excludes OAuth flows and third-party SSO.'

scope_in.description: Items explicitly included across all milestones. Each string should name a concrete capability, endpoint, or system boundary. The drift check (E308) uses this to detect milestone scope contradictions.

items.description: A concrete scope item included in this implementation.

scope_out.description: Items explicitly excluded from all milestones. The drift check (E308) fires if a milestone's scope_in contradicts this list.

items.description: A concrete scope item excluded from this implementation.

target_file_patterns.description: Glob patterns for files touched across all milestones. Optional on the anchor; each milestone plan carries its own target_file_patterns.

items.description: A glob pattern identifying files in scope.

ambiguities.description: Accumulated unresolved decisions and ambiguities across all Trinity cycles. Item shape is intentionally narrower than emergent_ambiguities in 16b (no `source` field) and planning ambiguities in 16a (severity uses severityLevel, not blocking/non_blocking) — the anchor carries cross-milestone decisions only. Populated incrementally as ambiguities surface; an empty array on a fresh anchor is valid.

items.description: A cross-milestone ambiguity or unresolved architectural decision.

id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this ambiguity.

description.description: Description of the ambiguity and what decision is needed.

severity.description: Severity: 'low' (clarification only), 'medium' (needs resolution before next cycle), 'high' (blocks milestone), 'critical' (may require spec revision).

impact.description: Areas or milestones affected by this ambiguity.

status.description: Current resolution status. Uses the shared ambiguityStatus atom — same enum as planning ambiguities and emergent_ambiguities.

status_ref.description: Canonical reference for the resolution status.

drift.description: Drift monitoring schedule for the anchor. 'checks' records the drift checks that have been run across milestone cycles. An empty array is valid on a fresh anchor — populate as milestone plans are created and drift is monitored.

items.description: Description of a drift check performed or scheduled. Example: 'Verified ms-auth scope_in does not overlap anchor scope_out (2026-04-10)'.

checks.description: Drift checks performed or planned across milestone cycles. Each string documents what was checked and when.

milestone_index.description: Registry of all milestones covered by this anchor. Each entry declares which FRs/APIs a milestone owns and the checklist ID namespace it uses. Used by validators to detect cross-milestone FR ownership conflicts (E308) and checklist ID collisions (E309). An empty array is valid on a fresh anchor before any milestone plans are created.

items.description: A milestone entry in the anchor index.

milestone_id.description: Kebab-case ID matching the milestone_id in 14_roadmap.json.

context_path.description: Relative path to this milestone's 16a plan from either the repo root (with `spec/` prefix) or the spec directory root. Must point at a file inside `impl_context/` with a lowercase/underscore/digit filename ending in `.json`. Example: 'spec/impl_context/ms_auth_plan.json' or 'impl_context/ms_auth_plan.json'. The pattern is enforced because downstream validators (traceability_closure, step_16_anchor) read this path directly — a typo silently drops the plan from coverage and drift checks.

status.description: Lifecycle status of this milestone, reusing the shared milestoneStatus atom (the same enum 14_roadmap.json uses). Values: 'pending' = not yet started; 'in_progress' = currently being worked; 'done' = all checklist items satisfied and review verdict is 'verified'; 'deferred' = consciously postponed. Only 'done' milestones are exempt from FR ownership conflict detection — pending, in_progress, and deferred all participate.

items.description: A FR or API ID owned by this milestone.

fr_refs.description: FR and API IDs owned by this milestone. Array is a set — duplicates are a schema error. Used by E308 to detect the same FR being active in two milestones simultaneously.

checklist_id_prefix.description: SCREAMING_SNAKE prefix namespace for checklist IDs in this milestone's 16a plan (e.g., 'AUTH', 'PAYMENT', 'USER_MGMT'). Must start with an uppercase letter, may contain uppercase/digits, and underscore-delimited segments may follow but must each contain at least one character. Trailing underscores are rejected to prevent double-underscored IDs (e.g. 'AUTH__LOGIN'). Must be unique across milestone_index entries to prevent E309 collisions.

summary.description: One-line status summary for this milestone. Example: 'Auth token issuance — 3/5 checklist items verified, CI green'.
